science.title: Quantum blueprint maps a practical path to testing unusual entanglement
science.summary: Adrian Del Maestro knows how to engineer a quantum fingerprint. Rick Mukherjee has a gift for tuning atoms. Their combined expertise has taken a theory sketched out on paper and created a pathway for real experiments. The results, published in the journal Physical Review Letters, move a law-defying "mathematical oddity" ever so slightly up the technology readiness scale

science.title: Researchers reveal inner-core structural evolution of Typhoon Bavi using multisensor satellite observations
science.summary: Tropical cyclones frequently undergo rapid, complex structural changes within their inner cores, such as eyewall replacement and wind-field expansion, that strongly influence typhoon intensity and coastal hazards. However, capturing these multilayered transformations continuously from the ocean surface to the upper cloud tops remains a major observational challenge.

science.title: DNA at nuclear edges forms protective UV shield in developing roundworm embryos
science.summary: Inside the cell nucleus, DNA is arranged into neighborhoods, some of which are tightly packed and mostly inactive. This so-called heterochromatin typically associates with the nuclear lamina, a meshwork lining the inside of the nuclear envelope. This arrangement helps organize the genome and regulate gene activity. But how and when it forms during embryonic development has remained unclear.

science.title: Scientists pinpoint DNA copying 'traffic jams' impacting genome stability
science.summary: Creating an accurate copy of the genome—the entire length of DNA in a cell—is the fundamental step before cells can divide, the basis on which all life sits. Errors in that duplication process—including replication pauses—lead to natural genetic changes that underpin evolution, but also give rise to diseases such as cancer.

science.title: Mitsubishi Electric Research Lab CEO on How He Reached the C-Suite

It took Anthony Vetro nearly 30 years to climb the corporate ladder at Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories, in Cambridge, Mass. science.title: Ultracold atoms reveal first direct view of bound-pair motion in a fracton system
science.summary: Particles can generally move between neighboring sites in a crystal, a solid in which atoms are arranged in a regular, repeating pattern, or an optical lattice, an arrangement of laser-based traps that confines atoms. A strong potential gradient (i.e., a steep change in potential energy across a crystal or lattice) makes this ordinary particle hopping difficult and energetically costly.
